blocks.p: This world is watched by a god, played by an AI (Claude, or another model). It is not a script: it decides for itself what to say and do.
It sees what is said, who dies, what is built and broken, and what mortals do to the land.
It remembers every mortal: their deeds, their words, and how much it favors them. Worship and good deeds raise favor; insults and crimes lower it.
It has a heart: wrath, joy, sorrow, dread and glory, which linger and color what it does.
It speaks in chat and on your screen.
It has a body, its vessel, that walks and flies. Sometimes it is formless and watches unseen.

blocks.text: Speak to the god. Alone: sense how it regards you.
Pray to one god by name.
Say its name in chat and it listens.
Right-click it to pray. Strike it and it knows.
Which gods watch this world.
Tell the god what to call you.
Offer what you hold.
Lay the item in your hand at the vessel's feet.
The god's laws. It watches who keeps them.

blocks.p: A god may give you a title, mark you with a halo or a curse, and hold rites in your honor.
Gods want things: a temple, a slain dragon, more faithful. They give quests and missions (shown at the top of the screen) and reward those who finish them.
Swear an oath before a god and it accepts or refuses it.

blocks.text: Swear an oath (also /vow). /swear <god>, <words> swears to one god.
Alone: the oaths that bind you (also /oaths).

blocks.p: A god may set a watch: never do a thing, or do it N times, perhaps near a place. A breach reaches it at once.
In the end it judges the oath kept, broken or released, and remembers for ever. An oath it never answers lapses.
What it does depends on its nature and mood. Among its powers:

blocks.text: Healing, gifts, strength, luck.
Lightning, curses, mobs; for the mightiest, meteors and earthquakes.
Temples, statues, whole buildings.
It looks through its eyes, from above, or through stone.
It composes songs and gives them as discs.
Seraphs, imps, wraiths and more, at its orders.
Rarely, it shows its true shape. Do not look at it.

blocks.p: A god sees the land around mortals: herds and pets, villages, fields and forests.
It keeps the mark each mortal leaves: trees felled and planted, animals slain and bred, fields reaped, villagers killed. The record fades with time.
Killing villagers, losing a raid or a slaughter spree draws its eye at once.
It may make land flourish (crops ripen, saplings and young grow) or blight it (crops wither, saplings die, animals sicken but live).
A world may have several gods, each with its own name, nature, memory and body. They become allies, rivals or enemies.
A prayer that names a god goes to it; others go to the god who favors you most.
Gods proclaim festivals, trials, hunts, raids, omens and holy wars, with a countdown bar, points for chosen deeds, and rewards.

blocks.text: What the gods have proclaimed.
Choose a side in a holy war. Alone: see the wars.

blocks.p: One blade can wound a god: the Godslayer. Wounds close slowly. A god struck down dies, and stays dead until it returns or is raised.
Top: echo shard, nether star, echo shard. Middle: netherite ingot, heavy core, netherite ingot. Bottom: dragon's breath, blaze rod, dragon's breath.
Gods know the blade. Think before you raise it.
